title: stochastic-prefix-amplifier-and-mini-batch-fidelity-prober
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Motivation: production traffic exhibits short, correlated prefix variations (e.g., small user messages that change the KV cache hit pattern and token emission distribution). Existing workload runners either replay static prefixes or do heavy-weight randomized mixes that are expensive to run at scale. This PR introduces a lightweight stochastic prefix amplifier (SPA) that perturbs prefixes with controlled noise patterns and a complementary mini-batch fidelity prober (MBFP) to quantify how batching and KV cache priming affect tail latency and per-token cost. The goal is an inexpensive, reproducible harness that surfaces regressions in warmup behavior, KV cache effectiveness, and batch packing efficiency without adding long-running e2e experiments.

What this PR adds:
- A new SPA runner (bench/runners/spa_runner.py) that applies configurable prefix transforms (token-level jitter, synonym substitution map, and length-scaling) and emits sequence cohorts with tunable correlation coefficients.
- MBFP harness (bench/probers/mini_batch_fidelity.py) that runs many short mini-batches, collects p50/p95/p99 latency and token-cost deltas per-cohort, and computes a compact fidelity score (0..1) describing generation stability under micro-batching.
- Tiled histogram exporter (bench/reporters/tiling_histogram_exporter.go) that shards latency histograms by cohort and primer-length and writes compact delta rollups for downstream dashboards.
- Integration tests and lightweight CI jobs that run SPA+MBFP under a CPU mock and a tiny GPU container to verify correctness and nonregression.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement SPA runner and config knobs
- [x] Implement MBFP scoring and aggregator
- [x] Add exporter to telemetry pipeline with protobuf-compatible compact rollups
- [x] Unit tests covering deterministic transforms and scoring logic
- [x] Small e2e smoke in GitHub Actions (cpu/gpu matrix)
- [x] Docs: short README and example job in bench/recipes/spa_mbfp_example.md

Notes on design choices and tradeoffs: SPA deliberately avoids full semantic paraphrasing to remain cheap and deterministic; synonym substitution uses a small curated lexicon that is seeded from production prompt diffs (sanitized). MBFP focuses on short-lived mini-batches (<=8 requests) to stress KV priming and batch packing without needing full cluster capacity. The tiled histogram format compresses cohort deltas into a few hundred bytes which keeps CI artifacts small and dashboard ingestion fast.

Commits summary:
- 7 commits: initial SPA runner; add MBFP harness; histogram exporter; proto schema and serializer; unit tests; CI matrix; docs and example recipe.

Changed files (high level):
- bench/runners/spa_runner.py (new) - core generator and deterministic transforms
- bench/probers/mini_batch_fidelity.py (new) - fidelity scoring and aggregator
- bench/reporters/tiling_histogram_exporter.go (new) - exporter and writer
- bench/protos/tiling_histogram.proto (new) - compact rollup schema
- bench/recipes/spa_mbfp_example.md (new) - quickstart recipe
- tests/test_spa_runner.py (new) - unit tests
- .github/workflows/bench-spa-ci.yml (updated) - added cpu/gpu smoke matrix

Testing and CI: The PR adds a short CI job that runs the CPU matrix (fast) and an optional GPU smoke job gated behind a self-hosted label to avoid cloud GPU expense. Initial CI run: cpu matrix passed, gpu smoke failed once due to flaky kernel selection in the fake-gpu shim; fixed in commit 5 and rerun. Final CI status: pass.

Review thread (high level):
- Avery Chen: requested clearer boundaries between MBFP fidelity score and existing cost metrics; suggested renaming internal field to "mini_batch_stability" for clarity. Author replied and updated scoring docs + changelog.
- Miguel Ortiz: asked for tighter proto schema (removed unused buckets) and safety check when exporter writes artifacts to object storage; author added atomic-write and checksum.
- Priya Kapoor: requested additional smoke for variable sequence lengths; author added length-scaling tests to tests/test_spa_runner.py.
- Approval: Avery Chen and Priya Kapoor approved after changes; Miguel gave thumbs-up on proto cleanup.

Merge details: squash merge into main after approvals. No release blocker; flagged for follow-up metrics dashboard work (ENG-2027).

Related work and trackers: Linked Linear items ENG-1983 (prefix variance study) and ENG-2027 (dashboard integration). No linked JIRA.

Operational impact: Designed to be low-cost for CI (short runs and compact artifacts). Telemetry exporter writes compact rollups that the dashboard ingestion job will parse; this PR includes schema but not the ingestion consumer—dashboard work is tracked separately.
